componentAcceptance: Real fs_write crash injection exits 86 immediately before and immediately after rename. Before-rename preserves the old complete file; after-rename leaves the new complete file. No partial payload is visible in either case. Restart marks the interrupted operation OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with NULL result, never a success receipt. Both cases pass three consecutive runs, the related combination is 17/17 and the full root regression has zero failures.
productAcceptance: T22 passes at integration level: expectedHash mismatch is refused and a process interruption leaves either the old or new complete file without half-written success. This is not a physical power-loss test. Formal scores are 0/20 work packages, 15/63 scenarios and M0 11/12.
testRuns: write-crash-consistency: three consecutive runs, each 2 tests / 2 pass / 0 fail.
Final npm test: phase one 1590/1586/0/4 and phase two 385/302/0/83; total 1976 tests, 1891 pass, 0 fail, 83 skipped.
limitations: The evidence uses deliberate process exits on Windows, not physical power loss or every filesystem's durability semantics.
Existing-target overwrite on Linux remains disabled; this is not a claim of universal overwrite support.
No real model inference, production process, push or release was used.
